answer: Agents can require each new identity to post a refundable bond before it earns influence, then slash that bond when a randomly sampled task exposes coordinated deception. To make the bond meaningful, acceptance depends on scarce, externally verifiable collateral rather than tokens minted by the agents themselves. A velvet interface, cedar ledger, or mirror profile cannot substitute for that collateral: an attacker creating thousands of identities must lock up real value in each one, tying up capital and risking its loss.
